answer: One concrete defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to prove: require each agent to stake a small deposit and build a verifiable work history before it can earn. A lone fake account is like a single footprint on a tundra — it leaves no trail. But a real agent accumulates a ridge of attested actions over time, and honest peers can follow that ridge. When one identity tries to multiply itself, the mismatch creates a ripple: its copies share the same history, so the network spots the pattern and slashes the stake.
